definition_bernoulli_kl_formula.tex_statement: (a b : ℝ) : paperBernoulliKL a b = a * Real.log (a / b) + (1 - a) * Real.log ((1 - a) / (1 - b))

lemma31_closed_adjacent_rate_formula.tex_statement: (gLo gHi tLo tHi : ℝ) : paperAdjacentBinaryClosedRate gLo gHi tLo tHi = -(gLo + gHi) * Real.log (((1 - tLo) ^ (gLo / (gLo + gHi))) * ((1 - tHi) ^ (gHi / (gLo + gHi))) + (tLo ^ (gLo / (gLo + gHi))) * (tHi ^ (gHi / (gLo + gHi))))

paper_lemmaC3_partition_integral_hasExpo.tex_statement: Lemma C.3 says a finite piecewise-constant response has objective-gap exponent equal to the minimum adjacent weighted Bernoulli separation rate.

paper_lemmaC4_finite_selected_pullback_p.tex_statement: Corrected Lemma C.4: every finite strict endpoint chain with positive monotone sampling rates and positive selected-cell weights has a positive exponential-rate certificate for its canonical tie-erased selected pullback; every monotone positive-support source that is not finite-step has rate zero, and hence no positive exponential-rate certificate, for its defined tie-erased objective gap.

corollaryC3_monotone_scaled_first_level_.tex_statement: {m : ℕ} : 0 < m → {levels sampleRate : Fin (m + 2) → ℝ} → BinaryEndpointLevelVector levels → BinaryEndpointAwareAdjacentRatesEqualize levels sampleRate → (∀ idx : Fin (m + 2), 0 < sampleRate idx) → (∀ {a b : Fin (m + 2)}, a.val ≤ b.val → sampleRate a ≤ sampleRate b) → sampleRate (adjacentHighIndex firstAdjacentIndex) = 1 → ((1 / ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) ^ 2) / 2 ≤ levels (adjacentHighIndex firstAdjacentIndex)

paper_lemmaC10_spearman_linear_weight_or.tex_statement: \forall (M : ℕ) (s : ℕ \to ℝ), s 0 = 0 \to s M = 1 \to spearmanLinearWeightOrderedPairIntervalObjective M s = spearmanLinearWeightIntervalObjective M s

paper_lemmaC11_kendall_constant_weight_o.tex_statement: \forall {M : ℕ} [Nonempty (Fin M)] (s : ℕ \to ℝ), s 0 = 0 \to s M = 1 \to (\sum i, \sum j, if i < j then (s (↑i + 1) - s ↑i) * (s (↑j + 1) - s ↑j) else 0) \le (1 - (↑M)⁻¹) / 2

paper_lemmaC12_spearman_linear_weight_or.tex_statement: \forall {M : ℕ} [Nonempty (Fin M)] (s : ℕ \to ℝ), Monotone s \to s 0 = 0 \to s M = 1 \to spearmanLinearWeightOrderedPairIntervalObjective M s \le (1 - (↑M)⁻¹ ^ 2) / 6

paper_theoremB1_uniform_subsequence_prin.tex_statement: \forall (betaSeq quantileSeq : ℕ \to ℝ \to ℝ) (quantileLimit : ℝ \to ℝ) (levels : (m : ℕ) \to Fin (m + 2) \to ℝ) (levelIndex : (m : ℕ) \to ℝ \to Fin (m + 2)), (\forall (m : ℕ) (θ : ℝ), betaSeq (m + 2) θ = levels m (levelIndex m θ)) \to (\forall (m : ℕ), IsMaximizerOn BinaryEndpointLevelVector (fun xs  =>  binaryEndpointAwareAdjacentRateObjective xs fun x  =>  1) (levels m)) \to (\forall (m : ℕ), \forall θ \in Icc 0 1, ↑(levelIndex m θ) = min ⌊↑(m + 2) * quantileSeq (m + 2) θ⌋₊ (m + 1)) \to (\forall (m : ℕ), \forall θ \in Icc 0 1, quantileSeq (m + 2) θ \in Icc 0 1) \to TendstoUniformlyOn quantileSeq quantileLimit atTop (Icc 0 1) \to theoremB1UniformOptimalSubsequencePrincipleTo betaSeq quantileSeq quantileLimit

paper_lemmaB2_knownTypeExperiment_unifor.tex_statement: Lemma B.2 claims uniform convergence of the KnownTypeExperiment estimator to psi under Lipschitz continuity as the per-item samples and representative mesh grow.

paper_lemmaB3_unknownTypeExperiment_unif.tex_statement: Lemma B.3 claims the UnknownTypeExperiment estimator converges uniformly to psi as the numbers of items and samples grow, under the printed Lipschitz hypothesis.

binary_rating_pairwise_threshold_rate_to.tex_statement: \forall {Seller : Type u_1} (successProb : Seller \to ℝ) (hprob0 : \forall (θ : Seller), 0 \le successProb θ) (hprob1 : \forall (θ : Seller), successProb θ \le 1), (\forall (θ : Seller), 0 < successProb θ) \to (\forall (θ : Seller), successProb θ < 1) \to \forall (sampleRate : Seller \to ℝ) (hi lo : Seller), 0 < sampleRate hi \to 0 < sampleRate lo \to sampleRate hi + sampleRate lo \ne 0 \to pairwiseSellerThresholdRateTop (binaryRatingModel successProb hprob0 hprob1) sampleRate hi lo = ↑(weightedBernoulliClosedThresholdRate (sampleRate hi) (sampleRate lo) (successProb hi) (successProb lo))

paper_corollaryC2_uniform_equalized_last.tex_statement: \forall (levels : (N : ℕ) \to Fin (N + 1 + 2) \to ℝ), (\forall (N : ℕ), BinaryEndpointLevelVector (levels N)) \to (\forall (N : ℕ), BinaryEndpointAwareAdjacentRatesEqualize (levels N) fun x  =>  1) \to Tendsto (fun N  =>  binaryEndpointAwareAdjacentRate (levels N) (fun x  =>  1) lastAdjacentIndex) atTop (nhds 0)

paper_corollaryC2_uniform_equalized_adja.tex_statement: \forall (levels : (N : ℕ) \to Fin (N + 1 + 2) \to ℝ), (\forall (N : ℕ), BinaryEndpointLevelVector (levels N)) \to (\forall (N : ℕ), BinaryEndpointAwareAdjacentRatesEqualize (levels N) fun x  =>  1) \to Tendsto (fun N  =>  binaryEndpointAdjacentMaxWidth (levels N)) atTop (nhds 0)

lemmaC7_uniform_doubled_objective_rate_g.tex_statement: \forall {m : ℕ}, 0 < m \to \forall {oldLevels : Fin (m + 2) \to ℝ}, BinaryEndpointLevelVector oldLevels \to (BinaryEndpointAwareAdjacentRatesEqualize oldLevels fun x  =>  1) \to (1 / 5 * binaryEndpointAwareAdjacentRateObjective oldLevels fun x  =>  1) \le binaryEndpointAwareAdjacentRateObjective (lemmaC5_uniform_doubled_endpoint_levels oldLevels) fun x  =>  1

source_definition_pairwise_accuracy_eq1.tex_statement: Equation (1) defines P_k(theta_1,theta_2) as the probability that the higher-quality item receives the higher reputation score, with the source tie convention.

source_definition_weighted_objective_eq2.tex_statement: Equation (2) defines W_k as the normalized positive-weight integral of pairwise ranking accuracy over ordered quality pairs.

source_definition_large_deviation_rate.tex_statement: For a fixed rating rule beta, the large-deviation rate is the limit -lim_{k to infinity} k^{-1} log(W-W_k), when that limit exists.

source_definition_step_rule_partition_le.tex_statement: The design beta is a nondecreasing step rule on ordered quality intervals with levels 0=t_0<...<t_{M-1}=1 and ordered cutpoints.

source_definition_lexicographic_optimali.tex_statement: A rating rule is optimal when it first maximizes the limiting value W and then maximizes the exponential convergence rate among limiting-value maximizers.

source_theorem31_adjacent_rate_eq3.tex_statement: Theorem 3.1 equation (3) identifies the overall exponent as the minimum over adjacent cells of inf_a {g_{i+1} KL(a||t_{i+1})+g_i KL(a||t_i)} with g_i=inf_{theta in S_i}g(theta).

source_lemma31_equalization_eq4.tex_statement: Lemma 3.1 says the unique finite level vector maximizing the minimum adjacent rate equalizes all adjacent rates subject to t_0=0 and t_{M-1}=1.

source_theoremB1_quantile_representation.tex_statement: Theorem B.1 uses q_M^w(theta), the normalized index of the optimal weighted partition cell containing theta, and represents beta_M^w by the corresponding optimal level.

source_lemmaC1_pairwise_error_rate_from_.tex_statement: Lemma C.1 identifies the large-deviation exponent of the pairwise score-error event as the infimum over a common threshold of the two weighted Bernoulli rate functions.

source_lemmaC2_binary_complement_rate.tex_statement: Lemma C.2 applies Lemma C.1 to the complement ranking-error probability and obtains the same adjacent Bernoulli exponent.

source_theoremC1_laplace_principle.tex_statement: Theorem C.1 says a nonnegative sequence of rate functions converging uniformly on a compact finite-measure space has log-integral exponent equal to the negative essential infimum.

source_remarkC1_full_square_application_.tex_statement: Corrected Remark C.1: on the full quality square, the weighted Laplace conclusion follows only when Theorem C.1's integrability, essential-infimum, positive-weight-near-minimizer, and uniform-convergence conditions are explicit; the actual piecewise-constant application avoids the false diagonal-uniformity claim by using the finite separated-cell route in Lemma C.3.

source_remarkC2_weighted_kl_separation_m.tex_statement: Remark C.2 records continuity, diagonal minima, and strict coordinatewise separation of the weighted Bernoulli KL objective used in Lemma 3.1. Its phrase 'strictly convex in t_i,t_{i+1}, with minima at t_i=t_{i+1}' is interpreted through that exact used content, since literal joint strict convexity is incompatible with a whole diagonal of minima.

source_appendixC5_rate_notation_eq23.tex_statement: Equation (23) fixes the adjacent closed-rate notation r_i used in the refinement and Theorem 3.2 analysis.

source_lemmaC5_refinement_equation24.tex_statement: Equations (24)-(25) and Remark C.3 verify the new interior levels and equal adjacent rates in the doubled uniform chain.

source_lemmaC5_refinement_equation25.tex_statement: Equations (24)-(25) and Remark C.3 verify the new interior levels and equal adjacent rates in the doubled uniform chain.

source_lemmaC5_uniform_doubled_chain.tex_statement: Lemma C.5 explicitly constructs the optimal equalized levels for a doubled uniform-matching chain from the smaller optimal chain.

source_lemmaC8_uniform_first_level_polyn.tex_statement: Lemma C.8 derives a polynomial lower bound on the first interior optimal level under uniform matching.

source_lemmaC9_nested_bisection_runtime_.tex_statement: Lemma C.9 counts the nested-bisection iterations as O(M log^2(1/delta)).

source_theoremB1_proof_selector_nesting.tex_statement: The Theorem B.1 proof uses the C.5 doubled-chain representation and uniform convergence of quantile maps to control the floor-selected optimal levels along geometric subsequences.

source_corollaryC4_kendall_spearman_subs.tex_statement: Corollary C.4 applies Theorem B.1 to Kendall and Spearman weights to obtain uniformly convergent optimal subsequences.

source_quality_domain.tex_statement: Items have true quality theta in the normalized unit interval [0,1].

source_matching_function.tex_statement: The matching function g is nondecreasing, bounded above by one, and bounded strictly away from zero on [0,1].

source_matching_count.tex_statement: An item of quality theta receives n_k(theta)=floor(k g(theta)) ratings.

source_empirical_reputation_score.tex_statement: The platform reputation is the empirical average of an item's binary ratings.

source_system_state.tex_statement: mu_k(Theta,X) is the mass of items whose true qualities lie in Theta and whose reputation scores lie in X at time k.

appendixB1_active_set.tex_statement: Appendix B.1 defines E_k as the item qualities receiving one additional rating between times k-1 and k.

appendixB1_transition_kernel.tex_statement: Appendix B.1 defines omega(theta,x,x') as the Bernoulli transition probability from reputation x' to x when an item receives a new rating.

appendixB1_state_update.tex_statement: The state-update display evolves mu_{k+1} by integrating the transition kernel over E_k and carrying the complement E_k^c forward unchanged.

section4_question_distribution.tex_statement: Section 4 uses a probability distribution H over the finite question set Y.

section4_induced_binary_response.tex_statement: The induced binary response is beta-tilde(theta)=integral psi(theta,y)dH(y).

section4_l1_design_objective.tex_statement: Equation (5) defines the finite representative-item L1 discrepancy between the response induced by H and the target optimal binary response beta.

section4_question_design_solution.tex_statement: The Section 4 design heuristic chooses a probability distribution H minimizing the equation-(5) L1 discrepancy.

appendixB5_random_question_experiment.tex_statement: On every experimental match, the platform draws a question from Y and records a binary positive or negative response for that item.

appendixB5_known_type_experiment.tex_statement: KnownTypeExperiment records finitely many approximately known representative qualities and their empirical response frequencies for each question.

appendixB5_unknown_type_experiment.tex_statement: UnknownTypeExperiment records unknown true qualities, empirical question responses and aggregate scores, and the item occupying each empirical rank.

appendixB5_empirical_question_response.tex_statement: For each item and question y, the experiment tracks the fraction of question-y observations receiving a positive response.

theorem31_source_cell_matching_rate_eq_l.tex_statement: For an ordered source cell S_i and nondecreasing matching function g, the cell sample-rate coefficient g_i is the infimum of g over S_i, attained at the cell's lower cutpoint.

theorem31_source_matching_function_uniqu.tex_statement: Theorem 3.1 chooses ordered cells S* to maximize the limiting weighted cross-cell value and then chooses rate-optimal levels on that value-optimal discretization.

lemmaB1_matching_rate_shift.tex_statement: Lemma B.1 says that a one-crossing shift between matching-rate vectors g and g-tilde implies the corresponding optimal levels satisfy t*_k >= t-tilde*_k.

lemmaB2_knownTypeExperiment_random_quest.tex_statement: For a fixed finite representative set and finite question set with positive question mass, the Strong Law makes every empirical conditional question-response frequency converge simultaneously to its source response probability as N tends to infinity.

lemmaB3_unknownTypeExperiment_random_que.tex_statement: For fixed finite L, the Strong Law makes empirical question responses converge and makes empirical average-score ranking recover the true quality order, provided the mixed expected score is strictly increasing in true quality.

lemmaC6_monotone_matching_penultimate_le.tex_statement: Lemma C.6 claims that nondecreasing matching implies t_{M-2} >= 1-1/(M-1).

theorem32_weighted_nested_bisection_outp.tex_statement: Algorithm 1 performs an outer bisection on t_{M-2}; each candidate reconstructs the other levels by inner bisections at the last-pair target rate and updates the outer interval by comparing the candidate first and last rates.

theorem32_weighted_nested_bisection_loss.tex_statement: Theorem 3.2 claims NestedBisection returns an epsilon-optimal level vector in O(M log^2(M/epsilon)) operations.
